messages:
tanvi: Heads up — since ~09:04 UTC we're seeing streaming token stalls and RPC deadline hits for a subset of requests in gpupool-usw2b. p99 tail latency for streaming tokens spiked from ~120ms to 2.1s.

jordan: saw the alerts, digging in. Is it across all racks/azs or localized?

tanvi: Looks localized to nodes in rack r12 (usw2b). Non-streaming gen calls are fine. Streaming token sequences show pauses then a bunch of tokens arriving.

alex: that pattern (pause then burst) screams packet reordering/late arrivals to me. Any recent config/kernel/mtu changes?

sylvia: We pushed a kernel driver update to r12 last night to fix a NIC memory leak — it also toggles GRO/TSO defaults. MTU was left at jumbo 9000.

infra-oncall: Running a quick tcpdump on pod->pod path now. If someone can tail: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/stream-rr.pcap port 12345` (RPC port obfuscated)

jordan: Got a few packets. Filtered by flow, here's a short summary from tshark:
```
Frame 1: seq 1000
Frame 2: seq 1002 (arrived before seq 1001)
Frame 3: seq 1001
... multiple out-of-order segments, gap reassembly delays
```

alex: Yep — reordering. With gRPC streaming and our token-by-token flush, out-of-order TCP segments can produce head-of-line delays in the kernel TCP stack or trigger retransmit timers depending on offload state.

sylvia: Confirmed NIC offload differences on a subset of r12 hosts: GRO enabled + LRO toggled by driver. A mismatch between hypervisor and host offload settings can cause coalescing differences and reorder at the kernel level.

tanvi: Impact: user-facing stream stalls, model-level deadlines occasionally tripped and request retried (cost + throughput hit). We should triage mitigation and root cause.

jordan: Quick mitigation options: 1) Force disable GRO/LRO on affected hosts `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off lro off` (fast, low risk) 2) Move streaming traffic away from r12 using affinity routing (need config push) 3) Roll back driver update (bigger blast radius).

alex: Also can reduce continuous batching window so fewer tokens buffered server-side — temp perf loss but reduces tail amplification if packets reorder. Change is config-only and reversible.

infra-oncall: I can run `ethtool` on the 6 impacted nodes and report back. Planning to disable GRO first on one host as canary.

sylvia: If canary looks good (token stream latency returns to baseline), we'll roll to remaining hosts and then schedule a proper fix: driver update + consistent offload config across nodes. Also need to audit any auto-mtu/mtu-negotiation scripts.

jordan: Noted cost hit: we estimate ~8% extra tokens due to retries and repeat sends for retried streaming sessions. We'll track billing impact but immediate focus is availability.

tanvi: Can we also capture RDMA metrics? Some of these hosts have RoCE enabled — reordering can break RDMA ordering expectations. If RoCE queues are affected we might see NIC-level drops.

infra-oncall: Captured NIC counters: `ethtool -S eth0` shows increased rx_mismatch and rx_errors on the affected hosts. RoCE counters show some seq errors. Dump saved at `/var/tmp/r12-nic-stats.log`.

alex: That explains why some requests get retransmitted by the RDMA stack causing stalls. If RoCE is in use for certain inter-node transfers we should ensure control-plane traffic for token streams avoids RoCE VLANs until fix.

sylvia: Plan of action:
- Immediate: canary disable GRO/LRO on 1 host in r12 (infra-oncall)
- Short term: disable GRO across remaining r12 hosts (if canary good) + reroute streaming traffic away from r12 for next 24h
- Medium: roll a driver patch revert or vendor NIC firmware that fixes offload toggling, and enforce offload config via ansible
- Postmortem: audit change that introduced mismatch + add unit test in node image pipeline to validate offload/mtu consistency

tanvi: Assigning owners: infra-oncall -> immediate canary + roll, sylvia -> driver/firmware coord, alex -> runtime config to shrink batching window and add fallback to non-streaming path for critical customers, jordan -> perf/cost tracking and postmortem writeup.

infra-oncall: Canary done on host r12-node-03, disabling GRO/LRO...

eng-sre-bot: Deploy check triggered by infra-oncall: `disable-gro-canary` applied to r12-node-03 (status: success)

infra-oncall: Canary looks promising — p99 token latency back to ~130ms on that host and no deadline hits for ~12m. Rolling to other 5 nodes now.

tanvi: Good. After roll complete, let's keep traffic steering in place for 24h and schedule firmware work with vendor next week. Also add a monitor for rx_mismatch and RoCE seq errors to catch regressions.

jordan: I'll open the incident ticket and draft the postmortem template. Will add the cost estimate and customer impact summary.

sylvia: I'll push an ansible check to block future images that change offload defaults without explicit override.

alex: Runtime change rolled to prod with reduced batch window (30ms -> 16ms) as extra protection. Monitoring shows small throughput dip but steady latency.

tanvi: Thanks all. Will follow up in incident doc. :thumbsup:
